referents.why: 'Your waves' (second masculine singular): the addressee of the decree is the sea, personified. It is not a candidate.
First person 'I declared': the speaker, the LORD.
Second person 'you may come': the addressee of the decree is the sea, not a candidate.
Second person 'you will not add': the same addressee as cl1, the sea, not a candidate.
Third person 'someone will fix': an indefinite subject. The grammar names no agent, though the context suggests the LORD.

links.why: The 'then' runs from the speech to the saying, which reverses it. The saying's content is the speech.
'I declared' introduces what is said. The content link goes to the first said clause (R1).
'You may come this far' and 'not you will add': the English 'but no farther' is a plain waw in the Hebrew.
The waw joins what the boundary brings about, so it is not a plain and.
R4: the stopping of the proud waves is what the boundary brings about, so it is the earlier clause's result.

groups.why: The sender is the LORD. The builder gave a slot id (cl0s), which is not a candidate. No addressee is recorded because the sea is not a candidate.

cant_tell.what: Addressee of the turn (the sea, personified)
cant_tell.why: It is not a candidate, so no addressee member is recorded.
An indefinite third person. The text names no agent.
